weaknesses: The abstract overstates the generality of the claims regarding the improvement in perplexity on human texts without sufficient empirical backing.
The paper does not adequately address the limitations of the proposed method, particularly in terms of computational efficiency and scalability in real-world applications.
The experimental setup lacks a comprehensive comparison with state-of-the-art methods beyond the selected baselines, limiting the contextual understanding of the results.
strengths: The proposed framework, Daemon, presents a novel approach to decoding as direct metrics optimization, which is a significant contribution to the field.

The theoretical guarantees provided for the optimization problem enhance the rigor of the work and offer valuable insights into the relationship between the decoding distribution and human text alignment.
Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of Daemon across various metrics and domains, showcasing its potential for practical applications in text generation.
